seo.title: Kiln Studio | Pottery workshops in Bristol
seo.description: Learn to throw and handbuild with working potters. Small classes, all clay, glazes and firing included.

fields.heading: Learn to make pots you'll use every day.
fields.text: Small classes on the wheel and by hand, taught by working potters. Everything you make is glazed and fired here, in our own kilns.

fields.heading: This season's workshops
fields.intro: Six-week courses and one-day sessions. Clay, tools, glazes and firing are all included in the price.

fields.heading: Fired here, every week
fields.text:
Our two kilns run every Wednesday and Saturday. Your pots go in for a first bisque firing, come back to you for glazing, then go in again for the glaze firing.

From the day you make a pot to the day you take it home is usually three weeks.

items.quote: I'd never touched clay before. By week six I had a set of bowls I actually eat from.
items.name: Priya

items.quote: The teachers let you make mistakes and then show you exactly why the pot collapsed.
items.name: Tom

items.quote: Glaze day was the best Saturday I've had in months. I left with pages of notes and three test tiles I love.
items.name: Helen

fields.heading: Not sure where to start?
fields.text: Book a two-hour taster. If you enjoy it, we take the price off any six-week course.

seo.title: Workshops
seo.description: Six-week pottery courses and one-day sessions on the wheel, by hand and in glazing.

fields.heading: Workshops
fields.intro: Classes have eight places at most, so there's always a teacher nearby when the clay goes wrong. Choose a level that matches where you are now.

items.question: Do I need any experience?
items.answer: No. Courses marked Beginner start from the very first lump of clay. If you've made pots before and want to improve, choose an Intermediate course.

items.question: What should I wear?
items.answer: Clothes you don't mind getting muddy, and short nails if you're throwing on the wheel. We provide aprons and towels.

items.question: Can I take my pots home on the last day?
items.answer: Pots need two firings, so the last pieces are ready about two weeks after the course ends. We'll email you when they're out of the kiln.

items.question: What if I miss a session?
items.answer: Let us know and you can join the same session in another course that week, if there's a free place.

seo.title: About the studio
seo.description: Kiln Studio is a shared workshop for potters in Bristol, with two kilns, eight wheels and room to learn.

fields.heading: A working studio that teaches
fields.intro: Kiln Studio started in 2019 as a shared workshop for four potters. We began teaching when friends kept asking to have a go, and we still make and sell our own work in the same room where classes happen.

fields.heading: The room
fields.text:
We have eight wheels, two large tables for handbuilding, a glaze kitchen with twenty tested glazes, and two electric kilns.

Between classes, members rent shelf space and kiln time to work on their own pieces.

fields.heading: How we teach
fields.content:
Every class starts with a short demonstration, then most of the time is yours at the wheel or the table. We'd rather you make ten wobbly bowls than watch one perfect one.

We use one stoneware clay body and a small set of glazes that we know well, so what you see on the test tiles is what you'll get from the kiln.

fields.heading: Come and see the studio
fields.text: We're open for visits whenever there isn't a class on. Ask us anything about courses or membership.

seo.title: Visit and contact
seo.description: Find Kiln Studio on Wharf Lane in Bristol, check opening hours, or send us a question about workshops.

fields.heading: Visit the studio
fields.intro: We're a five-minute walk from Temple Meads station, on the ground floor with step-free access.

fields.heading: Ask us a question
fields.intro: We reply within two working days. To book a place, tell us which workshop you'd like.

workshops.title: Wheel throwing for beginners
workshops.summary: Learn to centre, open and pull up the walls of a pot. By the end you'll throw cylinders and bowls and trim their feet.

seo.title: Wheel throwing for beginners
seo.description: A six-week beginner course on the potter's wheel in Bristol. Clay, glazes and firing included.

fields.heading: What you'll learn
fields.content:
• Wedging and centring clay on the wheel
  • Throwing cylinders, bowls and a simple jug
  • Trimming a foot ring once pots are leather-hard
  • Glazing your best pieces in the final session

Each week builds on the last, so try to come to all six sessions.

items.question: How many pots will I take home?
items.answer: Most people keep four to eight finished pieces. You'll throw many more, but part of learning is choosing which ones to fire.

items.question: Is there homework?
items.answer: No, but members' practice sessions on Sunday afternoons are open to anyone on a course, free of charge.

workshops.title: Handbuilding: coil and slab
workshops.summary: Build pots without a wheel. Pinch, coil and slab techniques for planters, plates and lidded boxes.

seo.title: Handbuilding: coil and slab
seo.description: A six-week handbuilding course in Bristol covering pinch, coil and slab techniques.

fields.heading: What you'll learn
fields.content:
• Pinch pots and how to join them
  • Building tall forms from coils
  • Rolling, cutting and assembling slabs
  • Texture, slip decoration and glazing

A good choice if you'd like to make larger or more sculptural pieces.

workshops.title: Glazing and surface
workshops.summary: For people who already make pots. Mix and test glazes, layer them, and learn why they run, crawl or pinhole.

seo.title: Glazing and surface
seo.description: A one-day glazing workshop in Bristol for people who already make pots.

fields.heading: What to bring
fields.content: Bring up to six bisque-fired pots of your own, or use the test tiles we provide. Lunch isn't included, but there are good cafés on Wharf Lane.

workshops.title: Taster session
workshops.summary: Try the wheel and handbuilding in one relaxed session. If you book a six-week course afterwards, we take £45 off.

seo.title: Taster session
seo.description: A two-hour introduction to pottery in Bristol. Try the wheel and handbuilding in one session.

fields.heading: How it works
fields.content: You'll spend an hour on the wheel and an hour handbuilding, with a teacher for every four people. We fire your two favourite pieces and email you when they're ready to collect.

fields.heading: Pick a date
fields.text: Taster sessions run most Saturdays and Sundays. Send us a message with the dates that suit you.
